correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed the full symbolic transfer and variance argument. For the seven intervals in RESULT.md, the lengths in order are 2(beta-2), 6-2beta, beta-2, beta-2, 6-2beta, beta-2, beta-2, all strictly positive. With equal fifth and sixth source values, the positive-branch inverse falls in source 7 on target 1, sources 5–6 on targets 2–5, and source 4 on targets 6–7, with weight 1/2; the negative branch adds source values 1,1,2,3 on targets 3–6. This gives the claimed transfer chart and, after substituting rho and w, invariance and w-Lw=rho h. Integration gives stationary mass 1 and positive-branch mass 2/3. Integrating the Poisson identity gives mean-zero h; the stated w integrates to zero, and its integral over the positive side is [(beta-2)(30-6beta)+(4-beta)(18-6beta)]/81=4/27. Thus the h-w pairing is 4/27. With g=w/rho, the normalized transfer P satisfies (I-P)g=h and P(f composed with T)=f. The centered m=g-(Pg) composed with T is killed by P, so its time translates are pairwise orthogonal. Their sum differs from the centered occupation sum by a bounded telescoping term. Its own variance contributes O(1/n) after normalization and its cross term is O(n^-1/2). The limiting variance is ||g||^2-||Pg||^2=2(4/27)-2/9=2/27. The joint-positive interval (0,beta/2) has mass (beta+4)/18, giving covariance (beta-4)/18, and the derivative observable multiplies H by log 2 almost everywhere. This proves the result for the stated stationary density and open interval without an ergodicity, mixing-rate, or CLT assumption. The frozen checker tests the symbolic chart given the chart's entries; positivity of the lengths and the chart itself are justified here for all parameters, not by sampling.

value.rationale: This is a second-order analogue of a well-motivated known mean plateau, not just another calculation of the stationary density. The exact constant controls stationary finite-time derivative variability while the changing one-lag term establishes that individual temporal dependencies need not share the plateau. The bounded explicit transfer solution is reusable in this family and establishes the full interval without statistical extrapolation.
